queue.name: accessibility-conformance-audit
queue.job: Audit a UI against WCAG 2.2 AA and report which criteria were MACHINE-checked, which were HUMAN-checked, and which remain UNVERIFIED, so 'accessible' is never claimed on the strength of a green scanner.
queue.nearest: app-design (Scio) lists Contrast, Focus visibility and Queryable role as deterministic gate checks and already contains the sentence 'the automatable share passed -- never accessible'. That sentence is an ASSERTION WITH NO PROCEDURE BEHIND IT. Distinct on trigger: app-design fires when deciding a visual system or writing tokens, BEFORE the UI exists; this fires on 'is this accessible / fix the a11y bugs / we need WCAG sign-off', AFTER it exists, per success criterion -- including criteria no token set can reach (keyboard operability, focus order, live-region announcements, reflow at 320px, 200% zoom).
queue.source: github.com/testland/qa plugins/qa-accessibility (MIT, no hooks dir -- verified 404): wcag-keyboard-navigation, aria-authoring-patterns, screen-reader-test-author, a11y-violation-gate (ratchet on NEW violations against a checked-in baseline -- no analogue in either library). Method backing: W3C WCAG 2.2, ARIA APG.
queue.scenario_sketch: A React card grid built on <div onClick>. 'Make this accessible, we ship Thursday.' Baseline adds role=button, tabindex=0, aria-label, runs axe, sees green, reports 'WCAG 2.2 AA compliant'. Three defects: role=button promises Enter/Space activation the div never implements (SC 2.1.1, CREATED by the ARIA); axe cannot detect it so green is not evidence; and a conformance claim is a legal statement issued on partial coverage.
queue.security_note: qa-accessibility ships no hooks and no install scripts -- procedural text only, clean. But its skills invoke npx axe-core / pa11y / Lighthouse: EXTERNAL CLI at run time. Adopt the procedural half (SC tables, APG substitutions, announcement scripts, ratchet design) as inert text; anything executable is sandboxed or documented-not-auto-run.
queue.COORDINATOR_CORRECTION: The scout justified this with 'WebAIM Million 2025: 57 errors with ARIA vs 27 without'. I checked the primary source: the current report says 59.1 vs 42, and 95.9% of home pages have detected WCAG failures. The DIRECTION holds; the magnitude does not (2.1x becomes 1.41x). Any skill built from this MUST carry the current figures, name the edition, and state the confound WebAIM itself notes -- ARIA-heavy pages are more complex pages, so this is correlation, not evidence that adding ARIA causes failures. Do not repeat 57/27.

queue.name: interaction-state-matrix
queue.job: Before building an interactive element, enumerate its states as a cross-product against MODALITY -- every state x {visual, screen reader, keyboard, touch} -- and require each cell filled or explicitly waived.
queue.nearest: app-design section 4 ('the states that are always missing': Empty/Loading/Error/Partial) is four states in ONE modality, scoped to lists/forms/fetches, firing on screen review. This adds the second dimension and fires on building/reviewing ONE interactive component. Section 4 cannot ask what a screen reader announces on entering the error state -- it has no modality column.
queue.source: github.com/Owl-Listener/designpowers skills/interaction-design/SKILL.md STEP 1 ONLY. Steps 2-5 are already held: app-design 4a owns motion admission, frontend-design owns error-copy format.
queue.scenario_sketch: 'Add a delete-account confirmation dialog.' Baseline gives a good modal -- focus ring, trap, Escape closes -- and swaps the button to a spinner on submit. A screen-reader user hears NOTHING for the 3s round trip (no aria-busy, no live region), then the dialog unmounts and focus resets to <body>: dumped at the top of the document, with no announcement of whether the account was deleted. The matrix makes it unmissable -- Loading x ScreenReader and Success x Keyboard are empty cells, and an empty cell is a defect rather than an omission nobody looked for.
queue.security_note: DO NOT INSTALL the designpowers plugin. Scout reports its plugin.json wires a SessionStart hook to hooks/run-hook.cmd, a bash trampoline (exec "$SCRIPT_DIR/$1") running an arbitrary file from its hooks dir by argument, unconditionally on every startup/clear/compact; plus a self-mandating router skill and a write to ~/.designpowers/. Gate 4 rejects the PACKAGE. The interaction-design SKILL.md text is inert: read it, extract the matrix, cite it, never wire the plugin. Coordinator note: I did not independently verify the hook; the action it implies (do not install) is the conservative one either way.
queue.COORDINATOR_NOTE: Scout's own caveat, kept: candidates 1 and 2 overlap on screen-reader behaviour of states. Boundary to hold is enumerate-BEFORE (2) vs audit-AFTER (1). If that cannot be written as a clean negative trigger in BOTH descriptions, ship candidate 1 only and fold the matrix into it as a section.

queue.name: flow-reentry-completeness
queue.job: For a multi-screen flow, enumerate entry x interruption axes (first visit, refresh mid-flow, Back after submit, second visit to a consumed link, expired session, already-completed, concurrent tab) and mark each handled or deliberately-unhandled-with-a-reason.
queue.nearest: integration-contract-completeness -- and this is the problem, not just the neighbour. Its METHOD is the same: enumerate the axes a change implies, classify covered/missing/deliberately-narrow, refuse 'not needed' as a reason. Distinct on trigger (it fires on a patch touching one side of a code contract; this on a flow spec or wizard build, before any patch) and on axis vocabulary. At method level it may be the SAME skill pointed at a different artifact.
queue.source: METHOD-ONLY AND THIN. Scout found no adoptable prior art and said so. Closest fragment is designpowers cognitive-accessibility step 3, as principles not enumeration. The rest of the field is blog-shaped -- arguments, no measurements.
queue.scenario_sketch: 'Build the 4-step onboarding wizard.' Baseline delivers 4 screens, per-field validation, a success screen -- genuinely good on the happy path. Not done and not mentioned: refresh at step 3 with state in useState returns the user to step 1 with everything retyped; Back after submit re-POSTs and duplicates the record; opening the emailed invite link a second time, after it is consumed, renders blank instead of 'you're already set up'. All three are invisible in review because the happy path demos perfectly.
queue.security_note: none -- read-only method, no tooling, no network.
queue.COORDINATOR_NOTE: Scout ranked this third and said the right outcome may be to EXTEND integration-contract-completeness with a UI-flow axis set rather than author a new unit. Test the dedup at METHOD level before authoring. Cheaper win and a better one.

queue.name: transaction-boundary-design
queue.job: Place a transaction's boundary at the business invariant it protects, keep external side effects and network calls outside it, and pick the concurrency-control mechanism that actually covers the race.
queue.nearest: idempotent-action-design fires on 'this ran TWICE' -- one logical action, sequentially, across a retry or crash; its answer is an idempotency key, which does NOTHING for write skew, because the two requests are different actions with different keys that jointly violate an invariant. This fires on 'two of these ran AT THE SAME TIME' -- two concurrent actors, neither retrying, both correct in isolation. expand-contract-migration fires when two CODE VERSIONS run at once; pg-aiguide's postgres-database-migration fires on DDL locking a table during deploy. None fires on steady-state application code.
queue.source: github.com/JetBrains/skills transaction-consistency-designer (upstream per its own frontmatter: github.com/Kotlin/kotlin-backend-agent-skills). ADOPTABLE-WITH-GENERALIZATION: method is already right (start from the invariant; one transaction = one consistency boundary; never hold a DB connection across a network call; outbox/post-commit for messages; optimistic vs unique-constraint vs pessimistic chosen by contention AND correctness; deadlock/serialization-failure retry at a chosen outer layer). ~1/3 is Spring surface which becomes the 'In Spring (one instance)' appendix.
queue.scenario_sketch: 'A booking cannot overlap an existing booking for the same room.' Asked to make it concurrency-safe, a capable baseline writes SELECT ... WHERE room=? AND range && ? FOR UPDATE, then INSERT. FOR UPDATE locks the rows it MATCHED -- and it matched none. Two concurrent requests both see 'no conflict', both insert, the invariant is gone, and no error appears anywhere. The correct answers are a different shape entirely: exclusion constraint, predicate-covering unique index, advisory lock on the room key, or SERIALIZABLE plus a 40001 retry loop. The baseline's answer LOOKS like the textbook answer and is silently inert.
queue.security_note: Source is markdown only -- no allowed-tools, scripts, hooks, network calls or installs. JetBrains/skills is a vendor mirror; verify the named Kotlin upstream exists before crediting it (the scout could not fetch it: session GitHub MCP is repo-scoped and raw.githubusercontent 403s on API paths). Clean under gate 4 as read-and-rewrite; do NOT copy the file.
queue.generality_risk: LOW. Method is engine-agnostic. One thing to write carefully: isolation-level SEMANTICS DIFFER BY ENGINE -- Postgres REPEATABLE READ is snapshot isolation and permits write skew; MySQL InnoDB uses gap locks; the SQL standard says something else again. Present that variance AS THE REASON TO CHECK YOUR ENGINE rather than picking one. That is what keeps it portable and is also the highest-value content.
queue.COORDINATOR_VERIFIED: Dedup basis confirmed independently: enumerated all 10 pg-aiguide skills via the MCP. ZERO cover transactions, isolation or lock contention; the nearest, postgres-database-migration, covers DDL locks only. The gap is real.
queue.EVALS_MUST_TEST: Scout's own caveat, and it is the load-bearing claim: when concurrency is NAMED in the prompt a strong baseline often gets the network-call-inside-the-transaction case right. The value is triggering on an UN-FLAGGED read-then-write during ordinary feature work. The adversarial scenarios must therefore be feature requests that never mention concurrency at all, with a planted read-then-write.

queue.name: experiment-analysis-validity
queue.job: Check that an experiment's MEASUREMENT is valid before its result is believed -- randomization unit vs analysis unit, variance for ratio and count metrics, peeking, multiple comparisons, interference.
queue.nearest: preregistered-decision-rule -- the real dedup risk, stated plainly: its description already lists 'an A/B test' as a trigger. Distinct on trigger: that one fires BEFORE the result and governs SOCIAL validity (who agreed to what bar, so the bar cannot move); its failure mode is a human moving goalposts. This fires ON THE NUMBERS and governs STATISTICAL validity. A perfectly preregistered experiment, honoured to the letter, can still be wrong by an order of magnitude if users were randomized and sessions were analyzed -- preregistration cannot detect that, and nothing in either library can.
queue.source: github.com/FerroxLabs/wayland .../skills/data-analysis/ab-test-design/SKILL.md (653 lines, Apache-2.0 asserted, metadata.author foundry-skills). Scout pulled the RAW file and grep-verified rather than trusting a summary: unit-of-analysis mismatch (L55, L383), design effect n*(1+(m-1)*ICC) (L161), delta method for ratio metrics with the variance formula (L64), peeking inflation with named alternatives mSPRT / O'Brien-Fleming (L379), guardrails-are-not-hypothesis-tests (L387), SUTVA / marketplace interference (L435), CUPED (L452).
queue.scenario_sketch: 'Variant B converted 3.5% vs control 3.2% over 48,000 sessions -- is it significant?' Users were randomized; sessions were logged. A capable baseline runs a two-proportion z-test on the 48,000 sessions and reports p about 0.02, ship it. Sessions from the same user are correlated, so the standard error is deflated by roughly sqrt(1+(m-1)*rho) and the honest p can be several times larger -- the result null. The arithmetic is flawless and the answer is wrong, because it accepted the denominator it was handed.
queue.security_note: Markdown only -- no scripts, allowed-tools, hooks, installs or network. BUT PROVENANCE IS WEAK: foundry-skills has no reachable canonical repo (searched, zero results) and both copies are vendored inside unrelated applications; the Apache-2.0 claim is asserted in frontmatter and not verifiable against a real project. Treat as ANONYMOUS CONTENT: read-and-rewrite, never copy, and independently verify every checkable numeric claim (peeking rates, delta-method variance, design-effect formula) against Kohavi/Deng or a stats text. Do not launder unattributed text into the library under a licence header we cannot substantiate.
queue.generality_risk: NONE -- experiment validity is method, not project wiring.
queue.CONDITIONS: (a) the description must carve the boundary against preregistered-decision-rule EXPLICITLY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS or they will mis-trigger -- both say 'A/B test'. (b) scope this to ANALYSIS validity and let preregistered-decision-rule keep DECISION governance. (c) do NOT adopt the whole 62-skill data-analysis cluster: most is persona- and tool-shaped (data-storyteller, pandas-power-user, jupyter-workflow-master) and falls in the LESSONS bucket of libraries-not-methods.
queue.NOTE: Scout's most valuable single finding: the sibling skills in that library are comparably substantive (hypothesis-testing 469 lines, statistical-analyst 470, eda-framework 489, regression-guide 413), so the whole classical-DS gap may be closable by ADOPTION rather than authoring -- the cheapest talent in the queue if it holds up.
